title: Walsingham letter-book, Nov 1572: Burghley and Walsingham letters with name codes, BL Harley MS 260 ff. 367-369 (DECODE R8361)

documents.shelfmark: BL Harley MS 260 ff. 367r-369v; DECODE R8361

plaintext.source: Letters printed in Digges, The Compleat Ambassador (1655) pp. 297-301 with the cipher left as figures; no decipherment found.

transcription.notes: Boxed digit codes [3] [7] [9], letter code H, one nine-sign letter run on f. 367r.

system.summary: Small name code of boxed digits and letters, plus a letter cipher of mixed digits and signs for one name; inserted in clear letters.
system.notes: Copy in a letter-book; the codes were copied from the sent letters.

prior_solution.where: Digges 1655 prints the letters but not the cipher's meaning; CSP Foreign x does not calendar them

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the six R8361 images with the DECODE cookie.
Identified pages as Walsingham's letter-book: Leicester, Burghley 7 Nov, Walsingham to Smith and to Burghley 27 Nov 1572.
Found all four letters in Digges 1655 pp. 297-301, cipher printed as figures; CSP Foreign x Nov 1572 has none.
Checked Tomokiyo's Elizabethan cipher page for a Walsingham 1570-73 key.
Code [3] fits 'the Queen' in all four uses.
Codes [7], [9], H and the nine-sign letter run: no consistent value.
Inventoried boxed codes in Digges 1571-73; 'Glasco [9]'/'Glasco [g]' show a box after a word marks a cover-name, so [9]/[7] after Florence, Rome, Glasgow are markers.
Retried all tokens with the marker reading; only [3]=Queen fixed; standalone [7], [9], H once each.

outcome.notes: Explained and in print; one code identified; the rest needs the key.
